features.name: DeviceRegistry contract (device keys, capacity, status, signer rotation)
features.summary: AccessControl contract where a registrar registers solar/wind devices with owner, meter signer address, capacity and lat/lon, can deactivate them, and can rotate the signer key.

features.name: GranularCertificate ERC-1155, one token per device-hour
features.summary: tokenId = deviceId<<32|unixHour. issue() and submitReadings() mint at most once per device-hour, only for finished hours, within capacity, and only with a valid device signature bound to chain and contract.
features.registry_match: One certificate per device-hour on-chain, retired by the hour

features.name: Device-signed hourly meter readings (ECDSA)
features.summary: The contract recovers the signer of readingDigest(chainid, contract, deviceId, hour, wh) and requires it to equal the registered device signer. The oracle signs with per-device keys, so there is real signature verification on-chain.
features.registry_match: Signed hourly meter readings per solar or wind device

features.name: Meter and fraud simulator (4 demo devices, 3 demo buyers)
features.summary: The readings are simulated from real Open-Meteo weather with AR(1) local-weather error and noise. Labelled tampering of four kinds (inflate, night_solar, flatline, replay) is injected, with one high-fraud device. Demo meter keys are derived deterministically from a text string. The README says meters are simulated.

features.name: Physics model of plausible output (solar PR/temperature derate, wind power curve)
features.summary: Computes expected Wh and a maximum plausible Wh per hour from irradiance, temperature and 100 m wind, with weather-uncertainty multipliers.

features.name: AI integrity check (physics bound + IsolationForest anomaly score)
features.summary: Per-reading features feed an IsolationForest. The learned signal is combined with a one-sided physics over-report check, a night-solar check and a replay check into a 0-10000 bps anomaly score with human-readable reasons. The score is evaluated against simulator fraud labels for precision, recall and false-positive rate.
features.registry_match: AI integrity check against Open-Meteo weather before minting

features.name: Quarantine of flagged readings and auditor release/reject
features.summary: Readings at or above the anomaly threshold (7000 bps, admin-settable) are recorded as Quarantined and hold the device-hour. An AUDITOR_ROLE holder can release (mint) or reject them permanently.

features.name: Hour-matched retirement and hourly match ledger
features.summary: retire/retireBatch burn certificates and credit the beneficiary for the certificate's own hour only. Buyer load is reported per hour, and hourlyMatchBps and periodMatch compute the capped hourly match.
features.registry_match: One certificate per device-hour on-chain, retired by the hour

features.name: ShiftReward (GSHIFT) ERC-20 incentive and surplus-hour bonus
features.summary: A minter-role ERC-20 that GranularCertificate mints to beneficiaries on retirement in oracle-flagged surplus hours (bonus per kWh).

features.name: Day-ahead GB carbon-intensity forecaster and surplus-hour picker
features.summary: A HistGradientBoostingRegressor uses lag features and wind/solar forecasts at four GB weather points, with a 7-day holdout MAE versus persistence and NESO. surplus_hours selects the cleanest 25% of hours.

features.name: Open-Meteo and UK Carbon Intensity API fetchers with disk cache
features.summary: httpx clients for Open-Meteo weather, the UK Carbon Intensity API (regional and national intensity, 48h NESO forecast), cached on disk by URL hash.
features.registry_match: AI integrity check against Open-Meteo weather before minting

features.name: End-to-end oracle pipeline (python -m gridproof.pipeline)
features.summary: Six steps: simulate readings, train and score the integrity model, register devices and submit batches on-chain, set surplus hours, report loads and retire proportionally per hour, then compute accounting and the forecast. Writes state JSON for the API.

features.name: Annual-style (volumetric) claim vs true hourly match, and hourly emissions accounting
features.summary: For each buyer the pipeline reads load and matched Wh from the chain. It computes the hourly match, a volumetric claim, and emissions as unmatched kWh times that hour's grid intensity, plus an all-grid baseline.

features.name: Device-level risk (near-top-of-band share)
features.summary: Per-device share of producing hours near the plausible maximum and share flagged, to point auditors at meters that inflate just under the per-hour check.

features.name: Web3 chain client (any EVM, local Hardhat or Sepolia)
features.summary: Python web3 client that signs transactions with the operator key, submits batches in chunks, reads statuses and certificates, and tracks gas and fees. It defaults to the public Hardhat test account on localhost and is read-only on public networks without a key.

features.name: FastAPI oracle API (/api/summary, buyers, readings, forecast, deployment, certificates, quarantine resolve)
features.summary: Serves pipeline state files plus live chain reads, executes auditor decisions on-chain via POST resolve, and mounts the built web dashboard. CORS is open to all origins.

features.name: Dashboard tab: Buyers, claim vs reality (match heatmap, intensity chart, hourly bars, GSHIFT tiles)
features.summary: Per-buyer comparison of the annual-style claim and the hourly match, with emissions and GSHIFT balance tiles, a day-by-hour match heatmap, a grid intensity line chart with surplus shading, and hourly use-vs-matched bars.

features.name: Dashboard tab: AI integrity check (metrics, per-fraud-type table, device risk, auditor queue)
features.summary: Shows fake-energy blocked, false-alarm rate, precision and recall, a per-tamper-type table, device risk, and an auditor queue with Reject/Release buttons that POST to the API.
features.registry_match: AI integrity check against Open-Meteo weather before minting

features.name: Dashboard tab: Clean-hour forecast
features.summary: Plots the GridProof model against the NESO forecast for the next 24h, lists recommended clean hours for flexible load shifting, and shows MAE versus baselines.

features.name: Dashboard tab: Verify on-chain (browser reads contract via ethers)
features.summary: The browser queries the Sepolia (or local) RPC directly, using ethers and the deployment ABI, to decode a token ID and show device, hour, status, energy, retired Wh, anomaly score and signer, with explorer links.

features.name: Hash-routed tab navigation
features.summary: Four tabs, each linkable via #buyers, #integrity, #forecast or #verify.

features.name: Hardhat deploy script (3 contracts, roles, ABI export)
features.summary: Deploys DeviceRegistry, ShiftReward and GranularCertificate, grants MINTER, ORACLE, REGISTRAR and AUDITOR roles, and writes addresses and ABIs to deployments/<network>.json.

features.name: Sepolia deployment record
features.summary: deployments/sepolia.json holds network, chainId 11155111, admin/oracle and the three contract addresses with ABIs. The README links the addresses as verified on Etherscan, Sourcify and Blockscout, which the audit did not check online.

features.name: Hardhat contract test suite (19 tests)
features.summary: Covers single issuance, forged or replayed signatures, capacity and future-hour limits, role gating, quarantine, retirement, the 100% match cap, GSHIFT payout, batches, deactivation and signer rotation.

features.name: Shell and Python ops scripts (demo.sh, deploy-sepolia.sh, serve-sepolia.sh, verify-sepolia.sh, new-wallet.py)
features.summary: demo.sh starts a local chain, deploys, runs the pipeline and serves the app. The Sepolia scripts deploy, serve and verify source on Etherscan/Sourcify/Blockscout. new-wallet.py generates a throwaway testnet wallet into oracle/.env without printing the key.

features.name: Docs: README, DEVPOST write-up, RUNNING guide
features.summary: Problem statement, architecture, results and honest limitations (simulated meters, testnet only), a Devpost submission draft, and run/deploy instructions.
